newsitem.title: ITALY: No Italy budget talks at Prodi meeting with allies.
newsitem.headline: No Italy budget talks at Prodi meeting with allies.

text.p: Parliamentary party leaders of Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi's Olive Tree coalition said on Tuesday they discussed parliamentary business with him at a meeting but did not talk about the upcoming mini-budget.

"We will finish off the end-of-year financial decree with a final vote," said Fabio Mussi, leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) in the lower Chamber of Deputies. The PDS is the biggest party in Prodi's centre-left coalition government.

"Then we will move onto the decree on transport. Finally there is this decree on the extension of terms," he said, referrring to a measure designed to re-regulate the transport sector and a technical decree covering measures about to lapse.
"We will see whether there are other possible routes than votes of confidence," Mussi said.
The government earlier won a vote of confidence in the Chamber to sweep away hundreds of opposition amendments to a final package of measures relating to the 1997 budget.
The vote was carried by 308 to 257, with one abstention. If a government loses a confidence motion it must resign.
Paolo Manci of the small centrist Italian Renewal party of Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told reporters "we did not speak about the mini-budget".
